review.notes: Reviewed and verified against VARK and Multiple Intelligences questionnaire sources with balanced 6-pathway coverage.

items.prompt: When learning a new topic, I understand best by reading written explanations, taking detailed notes, and expressing ideas in words.
When solving a problem or studying data, I prefer breaking it down into step-by-step logic, finding patterns, and working with numbers.
When I am learning something new, I prefer seeing information arranged in diagrams, charts, visual maps, and illustrations.
When I need to remember information, I prefer using tunes, rhythms, rhymes, or audio recordings to help the ideas stick.
When trying to understand how something works, I learn best by hands-on practice, assembling parts, and doing activities with my hands.
When studying real-world topics, I prefer observing living things, exploring nature, and classifying specimens into groups.
You are having trouble assembling a model or project that came in parts. What would you do?

options.label: Go through the step-by-step diagrams and exploded drawings to see how parts connect visually
Try arranging and handling the physical pieces to test how they fit together
Read the written assembly instructions and text notes carefully
Analyze the mechanical logic and interlocking order of the components

items.prompt: You want to learn about the plants and animals in a wildlife nature reserve. What would you prefer to do?

options.label: Observe animal habits outdoors and examine wild plant specimens directly
Listen to audio recordings of bird calls, songs, and natural forest sounds
Study color-coded maps, habitat infographics, and wildlife photographs
Read articles, printed field guides, and written descriptions of the wildlife

items.prompt: When investigating how environmental factors affect soil and water in your area, you would prefer to:

options.label: Collect samples with your hands, set up test tubes, and perform the physical experiment
Compare real soil types and plant growth outdoors in different natural surroundings
Calculate measurements, graph data points, and test cause-and-effect patterns
Listen to an audio podcast of environmental scientists discussing the findings

items.prompt: You want to learn how to play a new board game or strategy game with your classmates. You would:

options.label: Figure out the mathematical rules, scoring probabilities, and winning logic
Jump straight in, move the physical game pieces, and learn by trial and error
Study visual diagrams showing the board layout and strategic move pathways
Read through the full written rulebook and card instructions from start to finish

items.prompt: When learning how musical instruments and voices create sound waves and pitch, you prefer to:

options.label: Listen to melodic patterns, rhythm variations, and harmonic pitch differences
Look at visual waveform diagrams showing sound frequencies and amplitudes
Read a descriptive text explaining how acoustics and sound resonance work
Investigate how natural animal calls and hollow bamboo produce sounds in the wild

items.prompt: You want to understand how a complex bicycle or mechanical gear system functions. You prefer to:

options.label: Take the mechanism apart, adjust the gears, and test it with your hands
Calculate gear ratios and pedal revolutions to determine mechanical advantage
Listen to the rhythmic clicks and shifting sounds of the chain to diagnose it
Observe how animal skeleton joints and levers in nature mirror mechanical gears

items.prompt: You are exploring a new historic city or landmark for the first time. You would prefer to:

options.label: Use an illustrated visual map with landmarks, street layouts, and photos
Read written historic plaques, brochures, and guidebook articles
Walk through the streets and experience the physical setting firsthand
Listen to a walking audio tour narrated with ambient sounds and background music

items.prompt: When studying planetary orbits and solar system phenomena, you prefer to:

options.label: Compare planetary distances, orbital speeds, and temperatures in data tables
Study 3D visual models and star charts showing orbital paths
Memorize the planetary order using a catchy rhythmic song or mnemonic rhyme
Observe the night sky outdoors and track moon phases in the real environment

items.prompt: When learning new vocabulary and expressions in a language, what helps you most?

options.label: Read example sentences, write word definitions, and use written flashcards
Identify grammatical rules, word root logic, and sentence syntax patterns
Act out word meanings through gestures, role-play, and hands-on movement
Learn words for natural objects by observing plants, animals, and weather outdoors

items.prompt: You have to present an interesting school project to your classmates. You would prefer to:

options.label: Design visual posters with vibrant infographics, diagrams, and illustrations
Record a lively audio podcast with commentary, background music, and sound cues
Build an interactive hands-on model that classmates can touch and try
Write an engaging story or narrative article explaining the concepts clearly

items.prompt: When learning how animals survive in extreme desert or polar environments, you prefer to:

options.label: Examine animal fur insulation, feather structures, and real water-retaining plant adaptations
View colorful cross-section diagrams and geographic climate distribution maps
Analyze energy conservation formulas and temperature retention data
Listen to audio documentaries capturing wilderness soundscapes and animal calls

items.prompt: When exploring how energy flows through plants, herbivores, and predators in an ecosystem, you would prefer to:

options.label: Calculate percentage energy loss at each trophic level using a mathematical model
Trace producer and predator relationships by observing living species in a school garden
Participate in an active simulation passing energy tokens from sun to plants to animals
Read written case studies and field reports describing food web balances
